# AgentCake

> AI agent traffic analytics you run yourself: see which visits to your website are humans and which are AI agents
> (browser extensions, AI browsers, cloud agents, automated browsers), what each one did, and where a human took over.
> One program, one small database, no telemetry; open source under the MIT licence.

AgentCake answers questions such as: how do I detect AI agents visiting my website, can a website detect Claude in Chrome, how do I tell humans from AI agents in my analytics, and is there bot and agent analytics I can host myself. It records and explains; it does not block or challenge visitors. Every classification is made on the user's own computer or server, and no AI service is called.

An agent that moves and types like a human, with no name and no trace, can pass as a human; the evaluation report (eval/README.md) gives the current accuracy numbers.

To install it, a coding agent follows INSTALL.md one command at a time and then gives the user the local page, http://127.0.0.1:7878/. A public website's visitors need AgentCake on a server, as SERVER.md describes.

- [Questions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tartini-ai/agent-traffic-analytics/v0.6.0/docs/FAQ.md): detecting AI agents, Claude in Chrome, accuracy, privacy and how it differs from other tools
- [Server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tartini-ai/agent-traffic-analytics/v0.6.0/SERVER.md): running AgentCake for a public website's visitors, with Docker or systemd
- [Privacy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tartini-ai/agent-traffic-analytics/v0.6.0/PRIVACY.md): what is recorded, where it is kept and how to delete it
